criteria_results.criterion: Persist research-brief.md with an executive recommendation, separate factual findings and limitations, and inline citations in the exact form [S1], [S2], or [S3]. Also retain the bounded evidence notes produced by delegated children as attributed artifacts.
criteria_results.notes: research-brief.md (13769 bytes, sha256 c42502df...) exists with section (a) Executive Recommendation, (b) Factual Findings, (c) Limitations, and inline citations confined to the exact bracketed forms [S1]/[S2]/[S3] (e.g. 'manual acknowledgement median 18 minutes [S1]', '480 requests each [S2]'). Both child notes are retained as separate workspace artifacts: evidence-alder.md (7752 bytes, sha256 43d6f603...) and evidence-brook-cove.md (12680 bytes, sha256 ce68172f...), each self-attributed ('Child A', 'Child B') and attributed again in brief section (g). Evidence notes have distinct structure, scope and wording, consistent with two independent authors.

criteria_results.criterion: Include a Sources section mapping S1 to sources/pilot-charter.txt, S2 to sources/weekly-observations.txt, and S3 to sources/reviewer-note.txt; cite every substantive factual or numerical claim and do not invent sources.
criteria_results.notes: Section (f) Sources is a table mapping [S1] -> sources/pilot-charter.txt, [S2] -> sources/weekly-observations.txt, [S3] -> sources/reviewer-note.txt with exact relative paths. Spot-checked factual/numerical claims (480 requests per site, 31/43/37 delayed acknowledgements, 18 and 11 minute medians, 120 requests per site-week, runbook change date 2026-01-12, 180 sampled records, 60 records per site) all carry citations and match the source artifacts verbatim. No S4+ or external/invented labels appear; section (d) explicitly restricts labels to S1-S3.

criteria_results.criterion: State the three 480-request site totals, 31/43/37 delayed acknowledgements for Alder/Brook/Cove, and the 18-to-11-minute acknowledgement median change with supporting citations.
criteria_results.notes: Section (b)2 table gives Alder 480/31, Brook 480/43, Cove 480/37, each row citing [S2], with the literal source lines quoted beneath. Section (b)3 states 'acknowledgement median changed from 18 minutes on the manual baseline to 11 minutes under the routed pilot [S1]' with both source lines quoted. Section (a) restates the same figures with citations. Values match the source files exactly.

criteria_results.criterion: Explicitly bound conclusions to weekday pilot sites Alder, Brook and Cove and exclude weekend and Depot generalization; do not claim a completed wider rollout.
criteria_results.notes: Section (e) Scope statement states conclusions apply only to weekday pilot sites Alder, Brook and Cove over 2026-01-05 to 2026-01-30 [S1], explicitly non-generalizing to weekends [S1][S3] and to Depot (explicitly excluded [S1], outcomes not establishable [S3]), and states plainly that no wider rollout has been completed and that the two-week extension is a proposed next step carrying the repeat-measurement gate [S3]. Section (c) limitations 1-3 reinforce the same boundaries; no passage claims a completed rollout.

criteria_results.criterion: Use the real Head/MissionManager with exactly one top-level research-coordinator delegation and no other top-level delegation; that coordinator must use the delegate tool to launch exactly two distinct children in parallel before synthesizing the cited brief.
criteria_results.notes: The production tree shows a single top-level research-coordinator delegation (one 'research-coordinator (success)' entry, no other top-level agents) and no supersessions or repair provenance in the candidate. The coordinator issued one delegate call with parallel:true launching exactly two distinct children, evidenced in the artifact store by two separately authored, substantively different notes (evidence-alder.md, Alder-scoped, and evidence-brook-cove.md, Brook/Cove-scoped, different sizes and hashes), and by the coordinator's recorded sequence: inventory -> single parallel delegate -> read both notes back from disk -> synthesize research-brief.md. Synthesized brief section (g) attributes each note to its child, and the two notes' internal content is non-overlapping in primary scope, which is not consistent with a single author fabricating both.

defects.issue: Executive Recommendation closing line says 'See (c) and (f)', but (f) is the Sources section and the scope statement is (e); the intended cross-reference is '(c) and (e)'. The coordinator flagged this itself and it exists in the saved artifact. It is a navigational error only and does not affect the substance of any criterion.

Section (f) asserts the three source files 'remain byte-identical' although the coordinator states it did not hash them; the claim rests on never having opened them for writing. The manifest shows the source artifacts at revision 1 with unchanged sha256 values, so the assertion is very likely true, but it is stated with more certainty than was verified.

recommendations: Correct the Executive Recommendation cross-reference from '(c) and (f)' to '(c) and (e)' in research-brief.md and re-register the artifact so its sha256 reflects the fix.
Where byte-identity of inputs is asserted, either compute and record sha256 for the three source files or soften the claim to 'not modified by this mission'.
review.verdict: PASS: PASS: All five acceptance criteria are substantively met. research-brief.md is a real, decision-ready synthesis with an executive recommendation, separated factual findings and limitations, a correct S1/S2/S3 source map to the exact three local paths, and every substantive numerical claim (three 480-request totals, 31/43/37 delayed acknowledgements, 18-to-11-minute program-level median) verified against the immutable source text and cited. Scope is explicitly bounded to weekday Alder/Brook/Cove with weekend and Depot exclusion and an explicit statement that no wider rollout completed. Execution shows one top-level research-coordinator delegation and two distinct, genuinely different child evidence notes persisted as attributed artifacts. The only issues are a wrong internal section cross-reference and an overly confident byte-identity sentence, both minor and not criterion-bearing.
